author: Yuehua Wu
text: Abstract In this paper we explore the statistical properties of ratios of cumulative sums which frequently arise in various fields including time series analysis and econometrics We provide a systematic approach to approximating the moments of these ratios derived from the cumulative sums of independent and identically distributed random variables Leveraging techniques from asymptotic analysis and moment generating functions we present a framework that not only estimates the first two moments mean and variance but also offers insights into higherorder moments The central result is a series of explicit expressions that reveal how the moments of ratios scale with increasing sample size thereby highlighting conditions under which the approximations hold We validate our theoretical results through simulation studies demonstrating their applicability in empirical contexts The findings contribute to the understanding of the behavior of statistical ratios facilitating more robust inferential techniques in applied statistical practice This research serves as a foundation for further investigations into the distributional properties of cumulative sum ratios and their implications for hypothesis testing and confidence interval construction

author: Yuehua Wu

author: Yuehua Wu
text: We consider the problem of model or variable selection in the classical regression model using the GIC general information criterion In this method the maximum likelihood is used with a penalty function denoted by Cn depending on the sample size n and chosen to ensure consistency in the selection of the true model There are various choices of Cn suggested in the literature on model selection In this paper we show that a particular choice of Cn based on observed data which makes it random preserves the consistency property and provides improved performance over a fixed choice of Cn C Elsevier Science BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper investigates the solvability of a specific class of equations that emerge in the context of Mestimates a fundamental concept in robust statistics We begin by formally defining the class of equations under consideration and outlining their relevance in statistical inference particularly in the formulation of Mestimators which generalize maximum likelihood estimates Through a series of analytical techniques we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of solutions to these equations Our results reveal intriguing relationships between the properties of the underlying data distributions and the solvability of the associated equations We further explore implications of our findings for the consistency and asymptotic behavior of Mestimates To substantiate our theoretical results we provide simulation studies illustrating the practical significance of our work This research contributes to the understanding of Mestimates and offers pathways for further exploration in robust statistical modeling

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper investigates the rates of convergence of informationtheoretic criteria specifically the Akaike Information Criterion AIC and the Bayesian Information Criterion BIC in the context of rank determination for oneway random effects models We derive theoretical results that quantify how quickly these criteria converge to the true model rank as sample size increases By employing asymptotic analysis and techniques from statistical learning theory we establish bounds on the convergence rates and demonstrate how these rates are influenced by factors such as the number of groups the variability within groups and the distribution of the random effects Our empirical validation conducted through simulation studies highlights the practical implications of our theoretical findings showcasing scenarios where AIC and BIC display notable discrepancies in convergence The results provide valuable insights for applied researchers in selecting appropriate model ranks in oneway random effects structures ultimately contributing to more robust statistical modeling practices The implications of our findings extend to both theoretical and practical aspects of model selection in hierarchical and mixedeffects models

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we investigate the properties of L estimation methods in the context of censored linear regression models which are often encountered in survival analysis and other fields where data may be incomplete due to censoring We establish conditions under which L estimators exhibit consistency providing a theoretical framework that complements existing literature reliant on L or maximum likelihood estimation techniques Our approach utilizes techniques from convex analysis and leverages the geometric characteristics of the loss function associated with L estimates Through comprehensive simulation studies and real data applications we demonstrate that these L estimates not only maintain robustness to outliers but also converge to the true parameter values under certain regularity conditions Additionally we provide a comparison of the performance of L estimators against traditional L estimators highlighting significant advantages in terms of interpretability and resilience in the face of model misspecifications The implications of our findings extend to various disciplines enhancing the toolkit for practitioners dealing with censored data sets while ensuring coherent statistical inference

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper upper bounds on the probabilities of wrong determination of the rank of covariance matrix of random effects in oneway random effects models are given based on the information theoretic criterion Under weak conditions the bounds are shown of exponentialtype

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper addresses the complexities of discrimination analysis in scenarios where variates are grouped and observed in a sequential order Traditional methods of discrimination analysis often assume that data points are independently and identically distributed iid which can lead to biased conclusions when applied to datasets exhibiting group structures and temporal dependencies We propose a novel framework that integrates sequential analysis techniques with discriminant function methodologies to enhance classification accuracy in grouped data Our approach involves the modeling of variate dependencies through time series techniques while maintaining the integrity of discriminatory information We present a detailed examination of the statistical properties of the proposed method including its robustness against violations of standard assumptions Through a series of simulations and realworld applications we demonstrate that our model outperforms conventional methods in terms of predictive power and interpretability This study not only extends the theoretical foundations of discrimination analysis but also provides practical tools for researchers and practitioners dealing with sequentially grouped data in various fields such as epidemiology finance and social sciences

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper an informationbased criterion is proposed for carrying out change point analysis and variable selection simultaneously in linear models with a possible change point Under some weak conditions this criterion is shown to be strongly consistent in the sense that with probability one it chooses the smallest true model for large n Its byproducts include strongly consistent estimates of the regression coefficients regardless if there is a change point In case that there is a change point its byproducts also include a strongly consistent estimate of the change point parameter In addition an algorithm is given which has significantly reduced the computation time needed by the proposed criterion for the same precision Results from a simulation study are also presented C Elsevier Inc

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper an informationbased criterion for determining the number of clusters in the problem of regression clustering is proposed It is shown that under a probabilistically structured population the proposed criterion selects the true number of regression hyperplanes with probability one among all classgrowing sequences of classifications when the number of observations n from the population increases to infinity Results from a simulation study are also presented c Elsevier BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In the realm of statistical modeling the selection of an appropriate model is crucial for accurate inference and prediction This paper examines a class of model selection procedures that aim to optimize model performance while balancing complexity and goodnessoffit We introduce a comprehensive framework that categorizes these procedures into three main approaches information criterionbased methods crossvalidation strategies and Bayesian model selection techniques By applying extensive simulations and realdata examples we evaluate the efficacy of these methods across various scenarios highlighting their strengths and weaknesses in terms of bias variance and computational efficiency Furthermore we propose a novel hybrid approach that integrates elements from each method enhancing robustness and adaptability in model selection processes Our findings underscore the importance of contextdependent choice in model selection and offer practical guidelines for statisticians and data scientists seeking to navigate the complexities of model selection in empirical research

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In the realm of regression clustering accurately determining the number of clusters is a pivotal challenge that influences both model interpretability and predictive performance This paper proposes a novel consistent procedure for identifying the optimal number of clusters in regression clustering scenarios We first introduce a framework that integrates modelbased criteria with statistical techniques to assess cluster quality leveraging information criteria and crossvalidation methods to ensure robustness Our approach emphasizes the consistency of the cluster number estimation with increasing sample sizes thereby addressing common pitfalls in existing methodologies that may lead to overfitting or underfitting Through extensive simulation studies and realworld application on various datasets we demonstrate the efficacy of our method in accurately identifying the true number of clusters while maintaining the integrity of regression relationships The results show that our procedure outperforms current stateoftheart techniques providing a reliable tool for practitioners and researchers in the field of regression analysis and unsupervised learning This work contributes a significant advancement to the statistical literature on clustering by offering a systematic consistent approach tailored for regression contexts

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In many statistical applications it is crucial to identify points at which the underlying datagenerating process changes while simultaneously selecting relevant predictors that contribute to the model This paper introduces a novel framework for simultaneous change point analysis and variable selection in regression problems extending existing methodologies that consider either task in isolation We propose an integrative approach that leverages penalized regression techniques combined with a Bayesian change point detection mechanism This approach allows for the identification of multiple change points in the relationship between response and predictor variables while simultaneously estimating the most informative variables at each segment of the model Our method employs a hierarchical modeling strategy that facilitates the incorporation of prior knowledge and improves computational efficiency We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive simulations and illustrate its application through a case study on realworld data Our results indicate that the proposed method outperforms traditional techniques in terms of accuracy and interpretability providing a robust tool for analyzing dynamic systems in which both structural changes and variable importance are of interest

author: Yuehua Wu
text: AbstractIn the realm of statistical modeling the choice of the appropriate model is crucial to ensuring accurate inference and prediction Traditional model selection techniques often rely on fixed penalties that may not adequately reflect the unique characteristics of the data at hand This paper introduces a novel approach to model selection that incorporates a dataoriented penalty designed to adaptively reflect the complexity and structure of the dataset We present a framework that combines standard model selection criteria with a customizable penalty term derived from empirical properties of the data such as noise levels sample size and feature interactions Through simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate the superiority of our method over conventional approaches showcasing improved model fit while mitigating overfitting risks The proposed dataoriented penalty offers a more flexible and robust alternative for practitioners facilitating better decisionmaking in the model selection process Our findings contribute to the ongoing discourse on adaptive methods in statistics laying groundwork for further exploration into tailored penalties in various modeling contexts

author: Yuehua Wu

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we investigate the properties of minimum Lnorm estimators in linear regression models focusing on their strong consistency and convergence rates We establish that minimum Lnorm estimates commonly used for their robustness in the presence of outliers exhibit strong consistency under certain conditions on the design matrix and error distribution Our analysis reveals that these estimators not only converge to the true parameter values but do so at an exponential rate thereby addressing the efficiency aspect of Lnorm methods in practical applications We provide theoretical proofs and derive sufficient conditions to ensure these properties hold complemented by simulation studies that illustrate the performance of the proposed estimators relative to traditional least squares methods Our results contribute to the understanding of Lnorm approaches in regression analysis and offer insights into their operational effectiveness in realworld scenarios especially where data pollution is prevalent The findings underscore the viability of minimum Lnorm estimators as a robust alternative in regression modeling reinforcing their relevance in modern statistical practice

author: Yuehua Wu
text: There is vast literature on Mestimation of linear regression parameters Most of the papers deal with special cases by choosing particular discrepancy functions to be minimized or particular estimating equations A few discuss general results but prove results under heavy assumptions which seem to exclude important special cases In this paper a general theory of Mestimation is developed using a convex discrepancy function under what appear to be a necessary set of assumptions to develop a satisfactory asymptotic theory Detailed proofs are given for establishing the asymptotic normality of the distribution of Mestimates and the results are applied to several particular cases Appropriate criteria are developed for tests of hypotheses concerning regression parameters The problem is discussed in the multivariate situation which includes the univariate case

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper presents a comprehensive study of Ksample tests based on the likelihood ratio offering a robust framework for hypothesis testing in scenarios involving multiple independent samples Traditional approaches to Ksample comparisons are often limited by assumptions regarding distributional properties and sample sizes Our methodology leverages the likelihood ratio statistic as a powerful tool for assessing differences among K groups drawing on the principles of maximum likelihood estimation and advanced statistical inference We derive the asymptotic distribution of the likelihood ratio test statistic under both null and alternative hypotheses providing critical insights into test performance and power Additionally we perform a simulation study to evaluate the robustness of our proposed tests across various conditions including nonnormal distributions and unequal variances The results indicate that our likelihood ratiobased tests maintain superior power while controlling for Type I error rates under a range of practical scenarios We demonstrate the application of these tests through examples from fields such as medicine and social sciences where Ksample comparisons are frequently encountered This work not only enriches the statistical toolkit available for Ksample analysis but also addresses the challenges faced by practitioners in applied research Our findings suggest that likelihood ratio tests can serve as a reliable alternative for Ksample comparisons especially in complex data settings

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper introduces a segmented regimeswitching model designed to capture the dynamic behavior of stock market indices addressing the limitations of traditional linear models in depicting nonlinear market trends and volatility shifts By segmenting the time series into distinct regimes based on market conditions our approach enhances the understanding of market transitions influenced by economic indicators investor sentiment and geopolitical events We employ advanced estimation techniques including the ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm to efficiently identify regime boundaries and estimate model parameters from historical stock market data Through empirical analysis we demonstrate the models robustness and its superior performance in forecasting market fluctuations compared to conventional time series models The application of the segmented regimeswitching model to major stock market indices illustrates its effectiveness in identifying regimespecific characteristics and improving risk management strategies Our findings reveal critical insights into market behavior and provide a valuable tool for investors seeking to navigate volatile market environments Overall this study contributes to the literature on financial econometrics by offering a versatile modeling framework that can adapt to the complexities of stock market dynamics

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper investigates the limiting behavior of Mestimators for regression coefficients in highdimensional linear models specifically under the framework of scaleinvariant cases We derive asymptotic properties of these estimators focusing on their consistency and distributional characteristics as the dimensionality of the model increases Through a rigorous analytical approach we demonstrate that scale invariance significantly influences the convergence rates and the stability of the estimates We employ a combination of theoretical results and simulation studies to illustrate the practical implications of our findings in realworld scenarios characterized by highdimensional data Our results provide valuable insights into the robustness of Mestimators highlighting scenarios where traditional asymptotic results may fail and offering a framework for developing more resilient estimation techniques in highdimensional statistics The outcomes have implications for the fields of statistics machine learning and econometrics particularly in applications involving sparse regression and highdimensional parameter spaces

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we investigate the detection of a change point in the variance of measurement errors within a statistical framework Change points are critical in various fields including quality control finance and environmental monitoring as they signal shifts in underlying processes that may require intervention We propose a novel estimation method that leverages a combination of maximum likelihood estimation and sequential analysis to identify the point at which the variance of measurement errors undergoes a significant change Our approach is rigorously analyzed yielding asymptotic properties and convergence rates to quantify the efficiency of the estimate Through simulation studies we demonstrate the robustness of our method against various noise distributions and sample sizes highlighting its practical applicability in realworld scenarios Additionally we provide theoretical insights into the conditions under which the change point detection remains consistent and efficient Our findings contribute to the literature on change point analysis by enhancing the understanding of measurement error variance dynamics offering both theoretical advancements and practical tools for statisticians and practitioners alike

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper evaluates the ability of a Markov regimeswitching lognormal RSLN model to capture the timevarying features of stock return and volatility The model displays a better ability to depict a fat tail distribution as compared with using a lognormal model which means that the RSLN model can describe observed market behavior better Our major objective is to explore the capability of the model to capture stock market behavior over time By analyzing the behavior of calibrated regimeswitching parameters over different lengths of time intervals the changepoint concept is introduced and an algorithm is proposed for identifying the changepoints in the series corresponding to the times when there are changes in parameter estimates This algorithm for identifying changepoints is tested on the Standard and Poors monthly index data from to and the Nikkei monthly index data from to It is evident that the changepoints we identify match the big events observed in the US stock market and the Japan stock market e g the October stock market crash and that the segmentations of stock index series which are defined as the periods between changepoints match the observed bearbull market phases

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we introduce a novel estimator for conditional quantiles that incorporates auxiliary information enhancing the robustness and efficiency of quantile estimation in various statistical applications Traditional quantile regression methods can struggle with limited data or conforming to distributional assumptions however by leveraging available auxiliary variables our proposed estimator addresses these challenges We derive the estimators asymptotic properties demonstrating consistency and asymptotic normality under standard regularity conditions Utilizing a simulation study we compare our methods performance against conventional quantile regression techniques across multiple scenarios including varying degrees of noise and sample sizes Furthermore we illustrate the practical applicability of our estimator through a case study in econometrics where auxiliary information significantly improves quantile estimation for income distribution Our findings emphasize the value of integrating auxiliary information in quantile estimation providing a robust framework for practitioners seeking to make reliable inferences from complex data structures

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In the realm of statistical estimation the convergence properties of estimators play a crucial role in ensuring the reliability and accuracy of inferences drawn from data This paper investigates the necessary conditions for the weak consistency of minimum Lnorm estimates within the framework of linear models We begin by establishing the theoretical foundations of weak consistency and its significance in statistical practice particularly in scenarios characterized by highdimensional data and potential model misspecification Through rigorous mathematical analysis we derive sufficient conditions under which minimum Lnorm estimates converge in distribution to the true parameter values as the sample size approaches infinity We pay particular attention to the implications of design matrix properties and noise structure on the estimators performance Our findings illuminate the intricate interplay between the characteristics of the underlying linear model and the robustness of Lnorm estimation Additionally we provide simulation studies to validate our theoretical results and demonstrate the utility of minimum Lnorm estimates in practical applications The insights gained from this analysis contribute significantly to the understanding of robust statistical methods in linear modeling and highlight avenues for future research in estimation theory

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we develop a non conventional statistical test for the change point in a mean model by making use of an almost sure as convergence or strong convergence result that we obtain in respect of the difference between the sums of squared residuals under the null and alternative hypotheses We prove that both types of error probabilities of the new test converge to zero almost surely when the sample size goes to infinity This result does not hold for any conventional statistical test where the type I error probability ie the significance level or the size is prescribed at a low but non zero level eg The test developed is easy to use in practice and is ready to be generalised to other change point models provided that the relevant almost sure convergence results are available We also provide a simulation study in the paper to compare the new and conventional tests under different data scenarios The results obtained are consistent with our asymptotic study In addition we provide least squares estimators of those parameters used in the change point test together with their almost sure convergence properties

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper a new estimator for a conditional quantile is proposed by using the empirical likelihood method and local linear fitting when some auxiliary information is available The asymptotic normality of the estimator at both boundary and interior points is established It is shown that the asymptotic variance of the proposed estimator is smaller than those of the usual kernel estimators at interior points and that the proposed estimator has the desired sampling properties at both boundary and interior points Therefore no boundary modifications are required in our estimation C Elsevier Science BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this article an estimate of a change point in variance of measurement errors ME is given in terms of characteristic functions when the variances are known Its modification is also given for the case that the variances are unknown In addition the consistency and convergence rates of the estimator and its modification are investigated The simulation study shows that the proposed estimators perform well

text: General ksample tests are developed including the classical KolmogorovSmirnov Cramervon Mises and AndersonDarling ksample tests as well as new powerful omnibus tests based on the likelihood ratio Conventional tests are sensitive to location difference among distributions but are dull to detect the variation in shape The new tests are sensitive to both location and shape In fact if the distributions of ksampled populations are different in location only the new tests are as powerful as the old ones Otherwise they are much more powerful c Elsevier BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the Mestimation approach for estimating parameters in multivariate linear regression models with a focus on the application of convex discrepancy functions Traditional methods for parameter estimation such as least squares may be sensitive to violations of model assumptions and outliers prompting the need for more robust alternatives We propose a novel framework that extends Mestimation techniques by utilizing convex discrepancy functions to quantify the discrepancy between observed data and model predictions Our theoretical results establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the proposed estimators under general conditions We also provide a comprehensive simulation study that demonstrates the improved robustness and efficiency of our method compared to classical estimation techniques in various scenarios including the presence of outliers and nonnormal errors Additionally we apply our methodology to realworld datasets highlighting its practical utility in estimating multivariate relationships where traditional approaches may fail The findings underscore the advantages of using convex discrepancy functions within the Mestimation framework paving the way for more resilient statistical modeling in multivariate contexts

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we explore a novel statistical approach for detecting changepoints in the mean of a time series where we aim for methodologies that have almost surely zero error probabilities in identifying the point of change We introduce a new test statistic that combines empirical distribution functions with advanced resampling techniques allowing for robust detection under various conditions such as nonstationary behavior and the presence of noise We demonstrate that our proposed method achieves zero error probabilities in both the null and alternative hypothesis scenarios across a wide range of data distributions Through extensive simulation studies we illustrate the efficiency and reliability of our approach compared to existing methods confirming its practical applicability in diverse settings We further present realworld case studies to validate our findings and highlight the utility of changepoint detection in fields such as economics environmental science and quality control Our results underscore the importance of maintaining rigor in statistical testing while also providing a powerful tool for practitioners facing complex time series data

author: Yuehua Wu
text: The distribution of KolmogorovSmirnov statistic can be globally approximated by a general beta distribution The approximation is very simple and accurate It can be easily implemented in any statistical software Therefore we can use a beta distribution to find the practical pvalue of a goodnessoffit test which is much simpler than existing methods in the literature

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper investigates the challenges associated with density estimation in statistical settings particularly focusing on the conditions under which consistent estimates fail to exist We establish a framework that highlights the inherent limitations of conventional estimation techniques when applied to density functions exhibiting certain pathological properties By analyzing a series of illustrative examples we demonstrate that under specific conditions such as in the presence of heavily contaminated data or when dealing with highdimensional distributions traditional estimators do not converge to the true underlying distribution Our theoretical findings reveal that the nonexistence of consistent estimates stems from fundamental issues related to identifiability and the curse of dimensionality We further explore the implications of these results for practitioners emphasizing the necessity for alternative approaches to density estimation in problematic scenarios The paper concludes by proposing directions for future research aimed at reconceptualizing density estimation in the face of these challenges

text: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for General Mestimation extending classical estimation methods to a broader array of statistical models We establish foundational principles that govern the Mestimator approach focusing on the convergence properties robustness and efficiency of estimators derived from generalized estimating equations We introduce novel theoretical results that encompass consistency and asymptotic normality under various regularity conditions while also addressing practical challenges such as highdimensional settings and the presence of outliers Our methodology incorporates advanced computational techniques including gradient descent and penalized criteria to enhance estimator performance in complex scenarios We illustrate the applicability of General Mestimation through a series of simulations and realworld data applications demonstrating improvements in estimation accuracy and interpretability over traditional models Ultimately this contribution aims to provide researchers and practitioners with a versatile toolset for tackling a wide range of statistical inference problems paving the way for future advancements in empirical research

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper presents a novel beta approximation for the distribution of the KolmogorovSmirnov KS statistic which is widely utilized in goodnessoffit tests and nonparametric comparisons of sample distributions The KS statistic defined as the maximum distance between the empirical distribution function and the cumulative distribution function of a reference distribution is known for its sensitivity and effectiveness in testing the equality of distributions However obtaining the exact distribution of the KS statistic is often cumbersome leading to the need for accurate approximations We derive a highly efficient beta distribution approximation demonstrating its efficacy across various sample sizes and underlying distributions Through a comprehensive simulation study we assess the performance of our beta approximation against existing approaches including asymptotic and exact methods focusing on accuracy and computational efficiency Our results indicate that the proposed beta approximation offers a reliable and practical alternative for researchers and practitioners significantly simplifying the computation of pvalues associated with the KS statistic while maintaining robust performance across diverse scenarios We conclude by providing guidelines for its application in realworld settings and discussing potential extensions to other statistical tests Feel free to modify any part to better suit your paper or specific focus

text: AbstractIn the realm of statistical modeling the choice of the appropriate model is crucial to ensuring accurate inference and prediction Traditional model selection techniques often rely on fixed penalties that may not adequately reflect the unique characteristics of the data at hand This paper introduces a novel approach to model selection that incorporates a dataoriented penalty designed to adaptively reflect the complexity and structure of the dataset We present a framework that combines standard model selection criteria with a customizable penalty term derived from empirical properties of the data such as noise levels sample size and feature interactions Through simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate the superiority of our method over conventional approaches showcasing improved model fit while mitigating overfitting risks The proposed dataoriented penalty offers a more flexible and robust alternative for practitioners facilitating better decisionmaking in the model selection process Our findings contribute to the ongoing discourse on adaptive methods in statistics laying groundwork for further exploration into tailored penalties in various modeling contexts

text: We consider the problem of model or variable selection in the classical regression model based on crossvalidation with an added penalty term for penalizing overfitting Under some weak conditions the new criterion is shown to be strongly consistent in the sense that with probability one for all large n the criterion chooses the smallest true model The penalty function denoted by Cn depends on the sample size n and is chosen to ensure the consistency in the selection of true model There are various choices of Cn suggested in the literature on model selection In this paper we show that a particular choice of Cn based on observed data which makes it random preserves the consistency property and provides improved performance over a fixed choice of Cn C Elsevier BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: We consider the multiple regression model Yn Xn En where Yn and En are nvector random variables Xn is an nm matrix and is an mvector of unknown regression parameters Each component of may be zero or nonzero which gives rise to m possible models for multiple regression We provide a decision rule for the choice of a model which is strongly consistent for the true model as n The result is proved under certain mild conditions for instance without assuming normality of the distribution of the components of En

author: Yuehua Wu
text: Title On Strong Consistency Of A dimensional Frequency Estimation Algorithm In this paper we investigate the strong consistency properties of a novel algorithm designed for frequency estimation in twodimensional D data distributions The proposed algorithm employs adaptive sampling techniques to robustly estimate the frequencies of underlying components in scenarios with potentially high dimensional noise and varying spatial densities We formulate the conditions under which the algorithm converges almost surely to the true frequency distribution as the sample size tends to infinity Through a combination of theoretical analysis and simulation studies we establish the asymptotic behavior of the estimator demonstrating that it achieves joint strong consistency both in the estimation of individual frequencies and in the spatial structure of the underlying distribution Practical implications of our results are illustrated through applications in fields such as image processing and geographical data analysis where accurate frequency estimation is critical The performance of the proposed algorithm is benchmarked against existing methods showing superior accuracy and convergence properties Our findings contribute to the theoretical framework of statistical estimation in multidimensional contexts offering insights into the design of efficient algorithms for practical data analysis applications

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper presents a novel beta approximation for the distribution of the KolmogorovSmirnov KS statistic which is widely utilized in goodnessoffit tests and nonparametric comparisons of sample distributions The KS statistic defined as the maximum distance between the empirical distribution function and the cumulative distribution function of a reference distribution is known for its sensitivity and effectiveness in testing the equality of distributions However obtaining the exact distribution of the KS statistic is often cumbersome leading to the need for accurate approximations We derive a highly efficient beta distribution approximation demonstrating its efficacy across various sample sizes and underlying distributions Through a comprehensive simulation study we assess the performance of our beta approximation against existing approaches including asymptotic and exact methods focusing on accuracy and computational efficiency Our results indicate that the proposed beta approximation offers a reliable and practical alternative for researchers and practitioners significantly simplifying the computation of pvalues associated with the KS statistic while maintaining robust performance across diverse scenarios We conclude by providing guidelines for its application in realworld settings and discussing potential extensions to other statistical tests Feel free to modify any part to better suit your paper or specific focus

author: Yuehua Wu
text: The distribution of KolmogorovSmirnov statistic can be globally approximated by a general beta distribution The approximation is very simple and accurate It can be easily implemented in any statistical software Therefore we can use a beta distribution to find the practical pvalue of a goodnessoffit test which is much simpler than existing methods in the literature

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we prove that an algorithm proposed in Rao Zhao and Zhou gives a strongly consistent estimation of dimensional frequencies

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we investigate the properties of L estimation methods in the context of censored linear regression models which are often encountered in survival analysis and other fields where data may be incomplete due to censoring We establish conditions under which L estimators exhibit consistency providing a theoretical framework that complements existing literature reliant on L or maximum likelihood estimation techniques Our approach utilizes techniques from convex analysis and leverages the geometric characteristics of the loss function associated with L estimates Through comprehensive simulation studies and real data applications we demonstrate that these L estimates not only maintain robustness to outliers but also converge to the true parameter values under certain regularity conditions Additionally we provide a comparison of the performance of L estimators against traditional L estimators highlighting significant advantages in terms of interpretability and resilience in the face of model misspecifications The implications of our findings extend to various disciplines enhancing the toolkit for practitioners dealing with censored data sets while ensuring coherent statistical inference

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper investigates the solvability of a specific class of equations that emerge in the context of Mestimates a fundamental concept in robust statistics We begin by formally defining the class of equations under consideration and outlining their relevance in statistical inference particularly in the formulation of Mestimators which generalize maximum likelihood estimates Through a series of analytical techniques we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of solutions to these equations Our results reveal intriguing relationships between the properties of the underlying data distributions and the solvability of the associated equations We further explore implications of our findings for the consistency and asymptotic behavior of Mestimates To substantiate our theoretical results we provide simulation studies illustrating the practical significance of our work This research contributes to the understanding of Mestimates and offers pathways for further exploration in robust statistical modeling

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper the regression model with a nonnegativity constraint on the dependent variable is considered Under weak conditions L estimates of the regression coefficients are shown to be consistent

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we introduce a novel estimator for conditional quantiles that incorporates auxiliary information enhancing the robustness and efficiency of quantile estimation in various statistical applications Traditional quantile regression methods can struggle with limited data or conforming to distributional assumptions however by leveraging available auxiliary variables our proposed estimator addresses these challenges We derive the estimators asymptotic properties demonstrating consistency and asymptotic normality under standard regularity conditions Utilizing a simulation study we compare our methods performance against conventional quantile regression techniques across multiple scenarios including varying degrees of noise and sample sizes Furthermore we illustrate the practical applicability of our estimator through a case study in econometrics where auxiliary information significantly improves quantile estimation for income distribution Our findings emphasize the value of integrating auxiliary information in quantile estimation providing a robust framework for practitioners seeking to make reliable inferences from complex data structures

author: Yuehua Wu
text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce a robust and strongly consistent procedure for model selection in the context of regression analysis As the dimensionality of data continues to rise the challenge of selecting the correct model that captures the underlying relationships while preventing overfitting becomes increasingly critical Our proposed procedure leverages advanced statistical techniques to ensure not only theoretical consistency but also practical effectiveness across a variety of regression scenarios By utilizing a combination of penalization strategies and information criteria we establish conditions under which our model selection algorithm achieves strong consistency meaning it reliably selects the true model as sample size tends to infinity We provide rigorous proofs of consistency along with simulations and real data applications that demonstrate the superior performance of our method relative to existing model selection criteria The results suggest that our proposed approach is a viable and efficient solution for practitioners facing complex regression problems effectively balancing model complexity with predictive accuracy This work contributes to the ongoing discourse in statistical model selection offering a new perspective that emphasizes both integrity and robustness in decisionmaking under uncertainty

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In statistical modeling the consistency of parameter estimates is crucial for drawing valid inferences This paper investigates a necessary condition for the consistency of least absolute deviation L estimates in linear regression models We analyze the fundamental properties of the L estimation process particularly in the context of parametric assumptions and model design By establishing a link between the distribution of the error terms and the behavior of the design matrix we derive specific conditions under which L estimates converge to their true population values Through simulations and theoretical proofs we illustrate the implications of our findings for both wellspecified and misspecified models Our results contribute to the understanding of L estimation in the presence of potential outliers and nonnormal error structures providing a foundation for future research on robust statistical methods in linear regression settings These insights have significant applications in various fields including econometrics biology and social sciences where consistent estimation is essential

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In the realm of regression clustering accurately determining the number of clusters is a pivotal challenge that influences both model interpretability and predictive performance This paper proposes a novel consistent procedure for identifying the optimal number of clusters in regression clustering scenarios We first introduce a framework that integrates modelbased criteria with statistical techniques to assess cluster quality leveraging information criteria and crossvalidation methods to ensure robustness Our approach emphasizes the consistency of the cluster number estimation with increasing sample sizes thereby addressing common pitfalls in existing methodologies that may lead to overfitting or underfitting Through extensive simulation studies and realworld application on various datasets we demonstrate the efficacy of our method in accurately identifying the true number of clusters while maintaining the integrity of regression relationships The results show that our procedure outperforms current stateoftheart techniques providing a reliable tool for practitioners and researchers in the field of regression analysis and unsupervised learning This work contributes a significant advancement to the statistical literature on clustering by offering a systematic consistent approach tailored for regression contexts

author: Yuehua Wu
text: AbstractIn the realm of statistical modeling the challenge of selecting the most appropriate linear model is pivotal to ensuring accurate predictions and meaningful interpretations This paper presents an indepth exploration of linear model selection through the application of crossvalidation techniques We investigate various crossvalidation methodsincluding kfold leaveoneout and stratified crossvalidationto assess their effectiveness in identifying optimal models amidst a landscape of competing linear specifications By utilizing simulated and realworld datasets we evaluate the biasvariance tradeoff inherent in model selection processes emphasizing the robustness of crossvalidation as a tool for minimizing prediction error Our findings demonstrate that crossvalidation significantly enhances the selection process by providing a reliable estimate of model performance ultimately facilitating the choice of a model that balances complexity and accuracy We conclude with practical recommendations for practitioners and researchers regarding the integration of crossvalidation into their model selection workflows fostering more assured decisionmaking in linear modeling applications

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper a new estimator for a conditional quantile is proposed by using the empirical likelihood method and local linear fitting when some auxiliary information is available The asymptotic normality of the estimator at both boundary and interior points is established It is shown that the asymptotic variance of the proposed estimator is smaller than those of the usual kernel estimators at interior points and that the proposed estimator has the desired sampling properties at both boundary and interior points Therefore no boundary modifications are required in our estimation C Elsevier Science BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper an informationbased criterion for determining the number of clusters in the problem of regression clustering is proposed It is shown that under a probabilistically structured population the proposed criterion selects the true number of regression hyperplanes with probability one among all classgrowing sequences of classifications when the number of observations n from the population increases to infinity Results from a simulation study are also presented c Elsevier BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we investigate the convergence rate of the kernel density estimator KDE specifically for estimating the mode of a probability distribution Previous research has established the effectiveness of KDE in recovering global features of a distributions shape yet the asymptotic behavior at local extrema particularly around the mode remains less understood We focus on quantifying the rate of convergence of the KDE to the true mode as the sample size increases Utilizing techniques from both nonparametric statistics and asymptotic theory we derive upper bounds on the convergence rate in terms of the bandwidth parameter and the underlying densitys smoothness Our results demonstrate that while the convergence rate is highly dependent on the choice of bandwidth and the properties of the density function under appropriate conditions the KDE can achieve a convergence rate that is optimal for mode estimation Through simulations we illustrate the practical implications of our theoretical findings highlighting the influence of bandwidth selection on the accuracy of mode estimation This contribution not only adds to the understanding of KDE behavior around modes but also provides guidelines for practitioners in selecting appropriate bandwidths to enhance the estimation of local features in probability distributions Keywords Kernel density estimator mode estimation convergence rate bandwidth selection nonparametric statistics

author: Yuehua Wu
text: Let n n be an independent sequence with a mean shift We consider the cumulative sum CUSUM estimator of a change point It is shown that when the rth moment of Xn is finite for n and r strong convergence rate of the change point estimator is r oMnn for any Mn satisfying that Mn up arrow infinity which has improved the results the literature Furthermore it is also shown that the preceding rate is still valid for some dependent or negative associate cases We also propose an iterative algorithm to search for the location of a change point A simulation study on a mean shift model with a stable distribution is provided which demonstrates that the algorithm is efficient In addition a real data example is given for illustration C Elsevier BV

text: Let n be a sequence of independently distributed and nonnegative random variables and let Xn Sigmani Zi We show that under mild conditions E a Xnalpha can be asymptotically approximated by EXn alpha for a and alpha We further show that E bar fXnvertical bar can be asymptotically approximated by vertical bar EXnvertical bar for a function f satisfying certain conditions C Elsevier BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we investigate the strong convergence rates of estimators for change points in time series data building on the framework of statistical inference in the presence of structural breaks We introduce a novel approach that enhances the estimation of change points through a combination of advanced statistical techniques and computational algorithms Our results illustrate that under certain regularity conditions the proposed estimators achieve a strong convergence rate significantly improving the performance over existing methods in terms of consistency and accuracy We rigorously derive the asymptotic properties of these estimators demonstrating their effectiveness in various scenarios including boundary behavior and multiple change points To validate our theoretical findings we conduct extensive simulations and apply the proposed methodology to realworld data showcasing its applicability in fields such as finance environmental science and public health Our findings not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of change point detection but also provide practitioners with reliable tools for practical implementations The implications of our work extend to better decisionmaking processes in dynamic environments where change point detection is paramount

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper addresses the complexities of discrimination analysis in scenarios where variates are grouped and observed in a sequential order Traditional methods of discrimination analysis often assume that data points are independently and identically distributed iid which can lead to biased conclusions when applied to datasets exhibiting group structures and temporal dependencies We propose a novel framework that integrates sequential analysis techniques with discriminant function methodologies to enhance classification accuracy in grouped data Our approach involves the modeling of variate dependencies through time series techniques while maintaining the integrity of discriminatory information We present a detailed examination of the statistical properties of the proposed method including its robustness against violations of standard assumptions Through a series of simulations and realworld applications we demonstrate that our model outperforms conventional methods in terms of predictive power and interpretability This study not only extends the theoretical foundations of discrimination analysis but also provides practical tools for researchers and practitioners dealing with sequentially grouped data in various fields such as epidemiology finance and social sciences

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we investigate the conditions under which Maximum Likelihood ML estimates derived from the MLN model maintain statistical consistency The MLN model which extends the traditional maximum likelihood framework to accommodate hierarchical structures and dependent data presents unique challenges for ensuring the reliability of estimates We provide a comprehensive theoretical analysis detailing the convergence properties of ML estimates as sample sizes increase Through a combination of asymptotic theory and simulation studies we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the consistency of these estimates in various scenarios characterized by data heterogeneity and correlation Our findings reveal that factors such as model specification sample size and the underlying distribution of the data play critical roles in the consistency of MLN estimates We conclude by discussing the implications of our results for practitioners and researchers using the MLN methodology emphasizing the importance of adhering to the established consistency conditions in applied statistical analysis This work contributes to the broader understanding of likelihoodbased estimation techniques offering a robust framework for ensuring valid inference in complex data environments

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper we explore the asymptotic behavior of inverse moments of nonnegative random variables which possess significant applications in various fields such as finance reliability engineering and statistical inference We provide a comprehensive analysis of the conditions under which the asymptotic approximations of these moments can be effectively derived Utilizing methods from probability theory and asymptotic analysis we develop new results that refine existing approximations particularly in the case of heavytailed distributions Our findings reveal that the convergence rates of these approximations are influenced by the specific tail behavior of the underlying distribution We illustrate the applicability of our results through several examples and simulations demonstrating the practical utility of our approximations in estimating risk and variability in realworld data These results contribute to a deeper understanding of the properties of inverse moments and lay the groundwork for further research in the field of statistical inference related to nonnegative random variables

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In this paper the mode estimator based on the ParzenRosenblatt kernel estimator is considered In light of Shi et al under mild conditions we establish the relationship between the convergence rate of the mode estimator and the window width In this way we obtain a better convergence rate of the mode estimator C Elsevier BV

author: Yuehua Wu
text: In an earlier article Bai et al the problem of simultaneous estimation of the number of signals and frequencies of multiple sinusoids is considered in the case that some observations are missing The number of signals is estimated with an information theoretic criterion and the frequencies are estimated with eigenvariation linear prediction Asymptotic properties of the procedure are investigated but the Monte Carlo simulation is not performed In this article a slightly different but scale invariant criterion for detection is proposed and the estimation of frequencies remains the same Asymptotic properties of this new procedure are provided Monte Carlo Simulation for both procedures is carried out Furthermore comparison on the real signals is also given

author: Yuehua Wu
text: General ksample tests are developed including the classical KolmogorovSmirnov Cramervon Mises and AndersonDarling ksample tests as well as new powerful omnibus tests based on the likelihood ratio Conventional tests are sensitive to location difference among distributions but are dull to detect the variation in shape The new tests are sensitive to both location and shape In fact if the distributions of ksampled populations are different in location only the new tests are as powerful as the old ones Otherwise they are much more powerful c Elsevier BV

text: Chen and Wu proposed a conjecture on the consistency of the Minimum LNorm MLN estimator in linear regression models Here we prove two theorems showing that the conjecture is true under some circumstances

author: Yuehua Wu
text: AbstractIn this paper we address the challenge of simultaneous estimation of the number of signals and their respective frequencies in multiple sinusoidal mixtures particularly when faced with incomplete observational data Traditional methods often struggle with missing values leading to biased or inefficient estimates We propose a novel statistical framework that leverages advanced estimation techniques and optimization algorithms to recover both the number of sinusoidal components and their frequencies from partially observed time series data Our approach combines principles from Bayesian inference and the ExpectationMaximization algorithm to iteratively update estimates while accommodating missing observations We derive theoretical properties of our estimator proving its consistency and asymptotic normality under specific conditions Comprehensive simulations demonstrate the superiority of our method over existing alternatives in terms of estimation accuracy and robustness in various missing data scenarios Finally we apply our methodology to realworld datasets showcasing its practical utility in areas such as signal processing and biomedical engineering where missing data is commonplace This work contributes a significant advancement in the statistical treatment of sinusoidal signals amidst incomplete observations opening avenues for improved analysis in diverse applications

text: In this paper we introduce a novel estimator for conditional quantiles that incorporates auxiliary information enhancing the robustness and efficiency of quantile estimation in various statistical applications Traditional quantile regression methods can struggle with limited data or conforming to distributional assumptions however by leveraging available auxiliary variables our proposed estimator addresses these challenges We derive the estimators asymptotic properties demonstrating consistency and asymptotic normality under standard regularity conditions Utilizing a simulation study we compare our methods performance against conventional quantile regression techniques across multiple scenarios including varying degrees of noise and sample sizes Furthermore we illustrate the practical applicability of our estimator through a case study in econometrics where auxiliary information significantly improves quantile estimation for income distribution Our findings emphasize the value of integrating auxiliary information in quantile estimation providing a robust framework for practitioners seeking to make reliable inferences from complex data structures

author: Yuehua Wu
text: This paper presents a comprehensive study of Ksample tests based on the likelihood ratio offering a robust framework for hypothesis testing in scenarios involving multiple independent samples Traditional approaches to Ksample comparisons are often limited by assumptions regarding distributional properties and sample sizes Our methodology leverages the likelihood ratio statistic as a powerful tool for assessing differences among K groups drawing on the principles of maximum likelihood estimation and advanced statistical inference We derive the asymptotic distribution of the likelihood ratio test statistic under both null and alternative hypotheses providing critical insights into test performance and power Additionally we perform a simulation study to evaluate the robustness of our proposed tests across various conditions including nonnormal distributions and unequal variances The results indicate that our likelihood ratiobased tests maintain superior power while controlling for Type I error rates under a range of practical scenarios We demonstrate the application of these tests through examples from fields such as medicine and social sciences where Ksample comparisons are frequently encountered This work not only enriches the statistical toolkit available for Ksample analysis but also addresses the challenges faced by practitioners in applied research Our findings suggest that likelihood ratio tests can serve as a reliable alternative for Ksample comparisons especially in complex data settings
